Dev.releaseNotes:
`fix` (`media-info`): **Repair stored external subtitle languages and parse region-tagged names** ([#1452](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1452)):

The filename parsing fix in #1442 left three sources of unrecognized language errors.

- Added `RepairExternalSubtitleLanguages`, a one-time data fix that re-derives the language of external subtitle streams from their stored filename when the stored language is not shaped like a language code. Before #1442, the trailing text of the filename was stored as the language, and the stored media info kept it
- Accepted region-tagged suffixes such as `pt-BR`, `es-419` and `spa-ES` in `GetTrailingLanguageSuffix`, which were dropped before. The first part must be a known language, so suffixes such as `OP-NC` are not taken for one
- Stopped reporting the ISO 639-2 special codes `und`, `zxx`, `mul` and `mis` as unrecognized

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Move the provider configuration markers into `Config`**:

The interfaces that mark a configuration as a provider's own now sit with the
rest of the configuration contracts, and metadata providers got the one they
were missing.

- Added `IMetadataProviderConfiguration`, and constrained
  `IMetadataProvider<TConfiguration>` to it
- Moved `IAiringScheduleProviderConfiguration` from `Metadata.Airing` into
  `Shoko.Abstractions.Config`
- Made the bundled TMDb plugin's configuration implement the new interface

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.100**.

`docs`: **Match the READMEs and doc comments to the code**:

- Corrected the abstractions, plugin, queue, build tools and server docs where they contradicted the code
- Described the bundled TMDb and WebAOM plugins
- Wrote `null`, `true` and `false` as inline code in place of `<see langword>`

`fix` (`signalr`): **Let only admins pause or resume the queue**:

- Required admin for the aggregate hub's `queue.pause`, as the REST routes do
- Matched the explicit-provider release search default to its contract
- Registered the test sources when the test assembly loads
- Bumped `Shoko.BuildTools.Targets` to 0.3.2 in the bundled plugins

`feat` (`api`): **Bring the APIv3 TMDB surface back in line with upstream**:

- Ordered ratings, collection movies, suggestions, genres, episode groups and their credits as upstream did
- Let an ordering group carry its own season number, set from TMDb's group order
- Kept a movie's collection ID without its collection
- Listed episode-group specials in their regular group too, unless `includeSpecialsInSeasons` is off
- Fixed the zero page size, English-only biographies and the generic season name in a season's titles

`refactor`: **Synthesize titles, present episodes in their ordering and keep ordering texts in the text store**:

- Synthesized a default title for every stored entry without one, kept generic titles carrying the entry's own number out of the stores, and recognized more generic forms
- Added `CurrentOrdering` and presented a non-default ordering's episodes, groups and places in its numbering and titles
- Added `IMetadataOrderingService.GetEpisodePlacements` and `include=Placement`, for where each source places a special
- Moved ordering and group names and descriptions into the text store, and dropped their columns

`feat` (`queue`): **Rank jobs by priority within their pools**:

- Added `[JobPriority]`, `IQueueScheduler.EnqueueWithPriority` and the `QueuePriority` tiers, with scheduled actions above normal jobs
- Let immediate jobs skip the pool tier reservation, and raised, never lowered, a waiting job's priority on re-enqueue
- Ranked the core's jobs in the shared pools, and image, hash and media info jobs by purpose and file size, with a boost for new work
- Added `QueueProcessorSettings.DefaultPoolMaxWorkers`

`refactor` (`core`): **Cut the memory the caches hold**:

- Stored single-valued index keys without a set per row, and dropped the image indexes no hot path needs
- Pooled repeated strings in cached rows, media info and stored ordering IDs, and held a release's embedded data once
- Dropped the parsed XML docs once the server has started
- Brought a large metadata library's heap from 5.9 GB to 2.3 GB

`fix` (`api`): **Leave split movie parts a complete movie covers out of the missing episodes**:

- Grouped a movie's or OVA's missing episodes by their layout, as the series' missing counts already do, so the parts of a split film are not listed when its `Complete Movie` episode has a file (#1381)

Closes #1381

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Drop the default members that only forward to a typed member**:

- Removed the 27 default members of the typed metadata interfaces that only returned their typed counterpart
- Implemented the untyped members in the server classes that relied on them
- Dropped the `using` `IAnidbAnime` no longer needs

`refactor`: **Date episodes by their regular broadcast, and add `EarlyAirDate`**:

- Added `IEpisode.EarlyAirDate`; AniDB and Shoko episodes' `AirDate` gives the regular broadcast, with AniDB's own date as `EarlyAirDate` when it differs
- Removed `IAnidbEpisode.RegularAirDate` and `IAnidbAnime.RegularAirDate`; the regular start is episode 1's `AirDate` (`AnidbRegularAirDates.RegularStartOf`)
- Moved the matching engine and the TMDb plugin onto the regular dates

`fix` (`config`): **Keep constants and statics out of configuration schemas**:

- Built the `x-uiDefinition` structure from instance members only, so constants and static members no longer show up as settings
- Gave `SweepBudgetSeconds` and `RetentionMonths` their limits through `[Range]`, adding `MaximumRetentionMonths`

`feat` (`images`): **Support SVG images**:

- Recognized, validated and sized every image format, SVG included, through ImageMagick
- Accepted `image/svg+xml` on upload, download, `StoreFile` and the validation sweep
- Served stored images with `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP

`feat` (`api`): **Move the airing query filters into the service, and expose provider icons**:

- Added provider, episode type, collection, user, date-only and next-only options to `EpisodeAiringFilteringOptions`, replacing `ProviderID` with `ProviderIDs`
- Took `from`/`to` date-times with an offset in place of `startDate`/`endDate`, and let `IEpisodeAiring` carry date-only entries
- Exposed the service's configuration at `GET /api/v3/AiringSchedule/Configuration`
- Served provider icons at `/api/v3/AiringSchedule/Provider/{providerID}/Icon` and `/api/v3/Metadata/Provider/{providerID}/Icon`

`feat` (`api`): **Filter the AniDB anime list for season views**:

- Added season, type, collection and restriction filters to `/api/v3/Series/AniDB`, and `/api/v3/Series/AniDB/Seasons`, through `IAnidbService.GetCachedAnime` and `GetCachedAnimeSeasons`
- Listed an anime in every season one of its regular episodes airs in
- Picked each season's images from its best starter by weighted rating

`feat` (`api`): **Detect reruns, mark the preferred airing and estimate unlinked episodes**:

- Dated pre-1970 date-only airings from their linked episodes (`AnidbLinkedAirDateCache`)
- Added `EpisodeAiringKind.DetectedRerun`, the `EpisodeKinds` filter and hidden channels
- Added `IsPreferred` to airings, set on the one `PreferredOnly` would keep
- Estimated airings of episodes not yet linked to a schedule's source from an offset learned from the linked ones, only when most of them agree on it

`fix`: **Place series in yearly seasons by weeks, and tell AniDB's missing air dates from its placeholder**:

- `AniDB_Episode.AirDate` became nullable: `null` when AniDB gave no date, the 1970 placeholder restored from the cached XML
- Moved the episodes of a screening in several parts to their regular broadcast dates
- Seasons became whole-week runs with a lead-in (TV 4 weeks, others 1); an early premiere starts the next season, a batch drop gets no lead-in, and an entry carries over by the calendar quarters of its episodes, its last three left out

`refactor` (`api`): **Give the season view its own routes, with studios and genres from every source**:

- Added `GET /api/v3/AiringSchedule/Season/{year}/{season}` (`SeasonAnime`, next airing read on the server) and `GET /api/v3/AiringSchedule/Season`, replacing the season includes of `/api/v3/Series/AniDB`

- Added `CountryCode` to `IAiringChannel` and the channel key, and removed `GetRegionalChannelName`
- `FindOrRegisterChannel` matches own names, then aliases, then a same-named channel without a country

- Added `IAiringCalendarService` with season sections, calendar days and seasons by year
- Moved the season airing reads from `SeasonAnimeBuilder` into `AiringCalendarService`
- Added the `/api/v3/AiringSchedule/Season/{year}/{season}/Sections`, `/Season/ByYear` and `/Calendar` routes

`refactor`: **My fourth most evilest commit to date**:

Moved TMDb out of the core into a bundled plugin, brought the WebAOM renamer back as one too, and finished what the last one started. Every source, TMDb included, now keeps its data in the same shared tables, and the core no longer knows anything about TMDb beyond its API routes and the upgrade that moves its data over.

**Internal changes:**

- Moved TMDb into the bundled `Shoko.Plugin.Tmdb` plugin: its client, rate limiter, mapping, auto-linker, images, site pages, settings and actions. The upgrade copies the old `TMDB_*` tables into the shared `Metadata_*` tables and drops them, and moves the TMDb settings into the plugin's own configuration. Removed the `Shoko.Abstractions.Metadata.Tmdb` interfaces and services, and the core's `TMDbLib` dependency.

- Brought the WebAOM renamer back as the bundled `Shoko.Plugin.WebAOM` plugin, and moved the existing presets over to it.

- Typed series, seasons, episodes, orderings, movies and collections generically (`ISeries<TSeries, TEpisode>`, `IMovie<TMovie>`, …), so a source's own types come through without interfaces of their own, and gave suggestions their vote counts, approval ratings and scores.

- Placed specials in every ordering. Providers can say where a special airs, AniDB specials are placed by their titles ("Episode 6.5"), and every place in an ordering says what it airs before or after. Orderings also got their networks, which users' orderings carry through export and import.

- Added `IMetadataEntityProvider` for creators, characters, studios and networks. Entries a source names but hasn't stored yet are kept as stubs and refreshed by the provider that owns them. Entries now say when they were created, last updated and last refreshed, and movies, studios and creators got a few more fields (runtime, country, birthplace).

- Let providers pin an entry's default images through the stores (`DefaultImageResourceIDs`) instead of marking image candidates, kept every content rating a source gives, and resolved the site pages of every kind of entry, people and companies included.

- Kept a provider order per source and kind, so admins choose which provider answers for what, and let providers and image contributors name an icon.

- Made the completion threshold a setting (`CompletionThresholdPercent`, 95% by default), added a queue-cleared trigger for scheduled actions, and made metadata jobs show their provider, source, kind and ID in the queue in their display form.

- Gave the bundled plugins their thumbnails and icons, and made `DataType.Password` settings password fields in configuration schemas.

- **Broke the abstraction again.** The TMDb interfaces are gone, the metadata types are generic, `ImageCandidate.IsDefault` and the TMDb action category were removed, and suggestions changed shape. Plugins built against an earlier alpha need to be rebuilt, and the ones reading TMDb data need changes too. **Use at your own risk.**

**Changes in APIv3:**

- Kept the TMDb routes and models, now read from the shared tables. TMDb's settings and actions moved to the plugin, `IsLocked` is gone from seasons, generic episode titles ("Episode 6") are made for the ordering being shown, and the English title is the main one.

- Added per-source provider orders (`Metadata/Source/{source}/Providers`), source and provider icons, site URLs on metadata entries, creation and refresh dates on the metadata models, stubs and refreshes by hand for people, studios and networks, and the ordering choice on the generic metadata routes.

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.98**.

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Pause TMDB jobs while TMDB is rate limiting requests**:

- A 429 now pauses the TMDB jobs through `[TmdbApiRateLimited]` for as long as `Retry-After` asks, logged at Information
- The 429 and 5XX pauses share one deadline and `TmdbPauseReason`; the longer one wins
- One timer lifts either pause, re-armed when the deadline moves

`fix` (`api`): **Offer source and name pairs for `HasSourceGenre` and `HasSourceTag`**:

- Listed the (source, name) pairs each source has in `PossibleParameterPairs`
- Spelled the pairs' sources the legacy way, as `PossibleParameters` does

`fix` (`signalr`): **Join and leave aggregate feeds ignoring case**:

- Resolved the named feeds through `EventEmitterRegistry.Find` instead of a case-sensitive `Intersect`

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Never hand out seasons and episodes whose series is gone**:

- `TMDB_EpisodeRepository` and `TMDB_SeasonRepository` lookups by ID skip rows whose show row is missing, as do the TMDB listings in `MetadataService`; the series store and stored orderings skip entries whose series is missing
- `PurgeShow` and `PurgeMovie` remove the entry's own row last, so an interrupted purge leaves nothing without its parent
- The daily orphan purge refreshes each linked show or movie with no row, which stores it again

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Read TMDB's alternate orderings without a query per episode**:

- Indexed `TMDB_AlternateOrdering_Episode` on its episode, show, group and collection IDs; reading an episode's orderings was a full table scan
- `TMDB_AlternateOrderingRepository` and `TMDB_AlternateOrdering_SeasonRepository` are cached repositories now

`fix` (`db`): **Clear metadata leftovers on upgrade and refresh the linked ones**:

- added the `PurgeMetadataLeftovers` data fix, which runs TMDB's `PurgeLeftovers` and the new `PurgeStoreLeftovers` for plugin series whose row is gone, then makes the orphan purge due at start when linked entries are left for it to refresh
- the daily orphan purge also clears unlinked plugin series leftovers and refreshes the linked ones

`refactor`: **Split "Run Import" into dedicated scheduled actions**:

- Added `HashUnhashedFilesAction`, `ScanManagedFoldersAction` and `CheckForPreviouslyIgnoredFilesAction`
- Removed `ImportJob`, `RunImportAction`, `SearchForTmdbMatchesAction` and the `RunImport_*` methods of `ActionService`
- `SearchForMetadataMatchesAction` searches every source with an enabled auto-linker, TMDB included, picked through `GetAutoLinkers`
- The legacy `RunImport` routes and `Import.RunOnStart` queue the actions in order through `LegacyScheduledActions`, logging any that fails; the other legacy routes queue their matching action, and the TMDB-named searches stay TMDB-only

`fix`: **Search TMDB too in the per-series metadata auto-link**:

- `AutoLinkMetadataSeriesAction` searches every source with an enabled auto-linker, TMDB included
- A `Force` parameter, off by default, also searches the sources the series is left alone or already linked on and replaces their links

`fix` (`api`): **Require an admin to change a relocation preset's configuration**:

- `PUT` and `PATCH` `/api/v3/Relocation/Preset/{presetID}/Configuration` were open to every user
- The unmasked configuration of a preset whose provider is missing is shown to admins only

`fix`: **Show a restricted user every group holding a series they may see**:

- `AllowedGroup` and `IsAllowedToSee(IShokoGroup)` pass a group with at least one visible series; edits still need the whole group (`AllowedWholeGroup`)
- Added `AnimeGroupView`, the group as one user sees it, used by group-level filters, the v3 `Group` model, tree, filter, WebUI and APIv2 routes; a custom-named group keeps its own uploads

`fix` (`api`): **Keep sub-groups with files when `includeEmpty` is off**.

- Extras after a `+` or a space now stay with the `a`, `s` or `g` sub-item before them instead of becoming sub-items of their own
- An extra the entry does not take is refused as an invalid item

`fix`: **Write language keywords in descriptions as inline code**:

- `ShokoJsonSchemaGenerator` read the XML docs as Markdown, which turned
  `<see langword>` into a link to the keyword's documentation
- Added `WriteKeywordsAsCode`, used by `CleanDescription` and on every
  schema description

`fix` (`api`): **List a file when any of its series is visible**:

- Added `JMMUser.AllowedVideo`: a file with no series, or one the user may see, is kept
- The APIv3 and APIv2 file listings and searches use it, now also the managed folder files, duplicate files and recently added routes

`refactor`: **My third most evilest commit to date**:

Reworked how Shoko handles metadata. Every source is now a first-class citizen; plugins can bring their own, and the core stopped caring whether an entry came from AniDB, TMDB or somewhere else entirely. Also added scheduled actions, an actor behind every change, and databases for plugins, along with a few fixes here and there.

**Internal changes:**

- Replaced the `DataSource` enum with `MetadataSource`, a registry of sources the core and plugins register at start-up, and replaced the `DataEntityType` enum with `MetadataEntityType` for the kinds of entries. Every entry in the abstraction is now named by a `MetadataGuid` (`anidb://series/1234`), so `IMetadata.ID` is no longer a number for the most common types. Series, movies and episodes now carry `CrossSourceIDs` (through `IWithCrossSources`), the IDs other sources gave the same entry as far as the source knows them. And any entry can be looked up with `IMetadataService.GetEntry`/`IMetadataService.GetEntry<TMetadata>`, no matter which source it came from.

- Expanded the metadata provider system. TMDB is now just another provider, and plugins can add their own sources by implementing one or more of the provider interfaces: they can search, refresh, offer images and alternate orderings, and write their own series, movies, collections, people, tags, studios, relations and suggestions through the new typed stores in `Shoko.Abstractions.Metadata.Storage`. A plugin that keeps its data elsewhere can also answer through an `IMetadataResolver` instead of using the built-in stores.

- Added the shared cross-reference tables `CrossRef_AniDB_Metadata_Series`, `CrossRef_AniDB_Metadata_Movie` & `CrossRef_AniDB_Metadata_Episode`, written through the new `IMetadataCrossReferenceStore`. Removed the TMDB-specific links and entity lists from the abstraction in favour of the generic ones, which every series, season, episode and movie now carries, and added per-source getters for them, such as `GetSeriesCrossReferences<ITmdbShow>(MetadataSource.TMDB)` and `GetLinkedSeries<ITmdbShow>(MetadataSource.TMDB)`.

- Reworked auto-linking. Providers now return scored candidates, and the core decides, links and logs through `IMetadataLinkingService`, with a shared matching engine that lines series and episodes up by air dates, episode counts and titles. Started using AniDB's own TMDB and IMDb resources, and the links an anime already has to other sources, as hints. Links now remember their match rating, so added filters for series and movies with unverified links, and made every link exportable and importable as CSV.

- Added a universal text manager (`IMetadataTextManager`). Every title and overview from every source now lives in the same two tables, and users can pick, add, disable and remove them for any entry. Moved the names users gave their groups, series and episodes over as their own texts, and **renamed descriptions to overviews** everywhere in the abstraction.

- Added `IMetadataOrderingService` for alternate orderings of any series: global orderings a plugin provides, local orderings users make themselves, a preferred ordering per series, and hidden episodes. Moved TMDB's episode groups onto it too, and made orderings exportable and importable.

- Added image contributors, so a plugin can add images from its own source to entries of any source, core ones included. Gave images from every source the same per-source settings, and made an image a user uploaded win over the rest.

- Added databases for plugins through `AddPluginDbContext`. They live in SQLite next to the plugin's data by default, or inside the core's own MySQL or SQL Server database with prefixed tables, and the server migrates them during start-up, right after its own database. Also gave plugins their own configuration, data and cache folders.

- Added scheduled actions. Every recurring job in the core is now an `IScheduledAction` with default triggers (an interval, daily, weekly, monthly or at start-up) that admins can change, run by hand and cancel, and a run missed while the server was down runs once when it starts again. Also let queue jobs report their progress and be cancelled, and let waiting jobs be removed.

- Added an actor to (almost) everything. The API token behind a request is now the current actor (`IActorContext`) for the whole request, for SignalR calls, and for every job it queued. Configuration saves now say which settings changed and who changed them, user saves say which fields changed, and added events for plugins being enabled or disabled, API tokens being issued or revoked, and failed logins. All of this so a plugin can finally keep an audit log.

- Let plugins add their own feeds to the aggregate SignalR hub, and made the server keep track of why it needs a restart and tell admins about it.

- Did some smaller things along the way: SQLite databases are now compacted after an upgrade, AniDB resources are kept for every link type, `ReleaseStatus` and `SourceMaterial` are worked out for AniDB anime, episodes shown early are matched on their regular broadcast date, a plugin that can't load now says why, and the plugin loader picks the DLL that actually holds the plugin.

- **Broke the abstraction again, and a lot.** Beyond the renames above, IDs, sources, cross-references, orderings, texts and actions all changed shape. Plugins built against an earlier alpha need to be rebuilt, and most of them need changes too. **Use at your own risk.**

**Changes in APIv3:**

- Added generic `Metadata/{source}` routes to read any source's entries, manage its providers, and link Shoko series and episodes to it, and made `includeDataFrom` accept any source.

- Changed `MetadataSource` to be sent as its plain value (`anidb`, `tmdb`, …) instead of an enum name.

- Added `/api/v3/Text/Management` for the text manager, `/api/v3/Action/Scheduled` for scheduled actions, endpoints for users' orderings and hidden episodes, and queue endpoints to cancel and remove items and follow their progress.

- Exposed restart reasons at `/api/v3/Init/RestartReasons` and over SignalR.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Stop GetAniDBAnimeJob from busy-looping while HTTP banned**:

ProcessInternal already queues a rate-limited GetRemoteAniDBAnimeJob to
retry once the ban lifts, but it also unconditionally rethrew the ban
exception afterward. BaseJob.Process converts that into a
RequeueJobException, putting GetAniDBAnimeJob itself back on the queue
too -- but unlike GetRemoteAniDBAnimeJob, it isn't (and can't be)
[AniDBHttpRateLimited], since it can also run pure cache-only with no
network dependency at all. With nothing to hold the requeued instance
back, it re-ran instantly, hit the same ban, and requeued again,
forever -- filled a 116GB syslog in about 11 hours and took the disk to
0 bytes free.

Only suppress the rethrow once we've actually deferred to
GetRemoteAniDBAnimeJob, and only for AniDBBannedException specifically;
other exceptions still surface/fail normally.

`fix` (`api`): **Test an AniDB login against the stored password when none was retyped**:

`GET /api/v3/Settings` masks every secret on the way out, so a client that
posts back what it was handed, rather than what the user retyped, sends the mask
to `POST /api/v3/Settings/AniDB/TestLogin`, which used it as the password and
failed the login. The WebUI's AniDB tab does exactly that: it reads `Password`
out of the settings it fetched.

Saving was never affected, since the save path restores a masked secret before
anything reads it. This is the other kind of endpoint: one that uses a secret
without storing it, where there is no document to pair the mask against.

- Added `ConfigurationSecrets.Resolve`, which reads a mask as "the stored one",
  for any endpoint handed a secret it only uses
- Tested an AniDB login with the stored password when the caller sent a mask,
  and rejected the attempt when nothing is stored to test with

`feat` (`plugin`): **Tell each plugin once every plugin has been set up**:

`Setup` runs in load order, and a dependency always loads before the plugins
that depend on it, so a plugin that owns something other plugins contribute
to is set up before any of its contributors. Freezing a registry in its own
`Setup` would freeze it empty.

  already failed to set up

  comes up, and the boot stops with the plugin named

`RegisterPlugins` and `InitPlugins` on `IPluginManager`, though only the host
ever calls them. On the interfaces they read as the way to contribute, and
they were not: seven of the `AddParts` ignore every call after the first, so a
plugin's call did nothing, and `IImageManager.AddParts` replaced its list, so a
plugin's call dropped every resolver the other plugins contributed. Neither
said so.

  `IMetadataService`, `IAiringScheduleService`, `IVideoService`,
  `IVideoReleaseService`, `IVideoHashingService` and
  `IVideoRelocationService`, and `AddTransformParts`/`AddObserverParts` from
  `IVideoStreamPipelineService`
- Removed `ScanForPlugins`, `RegisterPlugins` and `InitPlugins` from
  `IPluginManager`
- Resolved each service through its interface in `PluginManager` and handed it
  its parts only when it is the implementation that takes them, and did the
  same for `RegisterPlugins` in `Startup`, so the registered service types are
  unchanged
- Gave `ImageManager.AddParts` the once-only guard the others have
- Said in the plugin README that implementing a contract is the whole of it

`fix` (`release`): **Enqueue the rescan that `TryScheduleRescanForVideo` builds**:

The method saved a new match attempt and built the provider chain, then
returned `true` without submitting it. `ScanForMissingReleaseInfoJob`
therefore never rescanned anything, and every sweep still inflated the
video's `AttemptCount`.

The chain is submitted with a plain `Enqueue` rather than
`EnqueueAfterCurrent`, since the caller is a recurring sweep over many
videos and each rescan jumping the queue would crowd out everything else.

`fix` (`release`): **Hand `SearchCompleted` the release a queued search found**:

`FinalizeReleaseSearchJob` raised the event without the release, so on the
queued path `ReleaseInfo` was always `null` and every search looked
unmatched to a subscriber, successful or not. The provider jobs have
already saved what they found, so a successful attempt's release is the
video's current one, and that is what is passed now.

`fix` (`config`): **Match masked secrets in lists by a keyed fingerprint instead of `[Key]`**:

`[Key]` is a display label in the WebUI: it can repeat and gets renamed, so
pairing list elements by it handed one element's secret to another whenever
two labels collided, and lost the secret when a label changed.

- Masked secrets now go out as `***SECRET-UNCHANGED:<fingerprint>***`, an HMAC of the value under a random per-install key
- Inside a list, a masked value is matched by fingerprint against the secrets stored for the same property, whatever element they sit on
- The key lives in `configuration-secrets.key` in the data directory, kept out of the settings file so a shared settings file cannot be used to test guesses offline
- `ConfigurationSecrets.Mask` and `Restore` take the key, and `IsMasked` recognises either form; the bare `Sentinel` is still accepted outside lists

`fix` (`plugin`): **Set a plugin up before the database, and record the failure instead of throwing**:

`SetupPlugins` ran from `LateStart`, which is after the database is opened,
and let the exception reach that handler. Both were wrong. A plugin should
take its services while the rest of the server is still ahead of it, and
throwing out of the start-up path skips the web host and lets the process
die with nothing left running to report why.

The failure is recorded where it happens and the boot is abandoned once the
web host is listening, so the server stays reachable in a state that names
the plugin that stopped it.

- Moved the call to right after `InitPlugins`, before any database work
- Recorded `StartupFailedException` rather than throwing, and returned the
  host once it is up instead of continuing into setup mode or `LateStart`
- Corrected the contract, which said `Setup` runs after the server is up

`fix` (`plugin`): **Make a failed `Setup` fatal once the web host can report it**:

`Setup` ran from `InitPlugins`, which happens before the web host starts and
before the hosted services a plugin registered, and a plugin that threw was
skipped. That skip could not work: services are registered into the container
before initialization and cannot be taken back out of a built one, so a
skipped plugin's hosted services still started. `Shoko.Plugin.Mcp` proved it
by taking the whole server down with a `NullReferenceException` inside
`ConfigurationService.Load`, because the configuration type it reached for
belonged to the plugin that had just been dropped from the exported types.

The fault has to be fatal, then, since it cannot be contained. Running it
late makes it a fatal the operator can read: the web host is already
listening, so `StartupFailedException` reaches the Web UI and names the
plugin instead of the process dying with a stack trace pointing at
configuration.

- Moved the call into `PluginManager.SetupPlugins`, invoked from `LateStart`
  after the session factory is up
- Let the throw reach `LateStart`'s handler, wrapped with the plugin's name
- Dropped the skip, and with it the disposal that only made sense while a
  plugin could be dropped and the server carry on
- Said in the contract that `Setup` runs after the server is up, that
  throwing stops startup, and that the hook only binds on recompile

`feat` (`plugin`): **Let a plugin acquire its services after the container exists**:

A plugin is built twice, and only the second build goes through the
container. Discovery builds it with `Activator.CreateInstance` to read its
identity, which needs a public parameterless constructor and throws without
one, so a plugin that took a constructor dependency never loaded at all and
failed with a `MissingMethodException` that named nothing useful.

`Setup` is the way in instead, mirroring `IQueueJob.Setup`, which exists for
the same reason. The default implementation is a no-op, so nothing already
written has to change.

- Added `IPlugin.Setup(IServiceProvider)` with an empty default
- Called it from `InitPlugins` on the instance the container built
- Skipped a plugin whose `Setup` threw, and disposed it if it can be, rather
  than leaving one loaded that never got what it asked for and would fail
  later somewhere that points nowhere near here

Note that a plugin only gets this on recompile: a `Setup` method compiled
against an abstraction that did not declare one is an ordinary public method
the runtime never maps, so it silently keeps the default. That also means no
existing plugin is hijacked by the new member.
